snippet.title: HF Antennas Low Down - Do Low Dipoles actually work.
snippet.description: Many hams have small gardens or small backyards. There may also be height or other restrictions.  This can seem to be a real challenge. Text books tell what we should aim for with regard to size etc.  What these books often do is frighten you into thinking that unless you can achieve  these recommendations, you have little hope of radiating a decent  signal. Well I can tell you that breaking these "rules" can be a bit of an adventure and for those prepared to take on the challenge, there can often be some surprising rewards. Peter G3OJV gives encouragement to those with lack of space for antennas.

snippet.title: What Happened to CB Linear Amplifiers? The Illegal Box Under the Seat
snippet.description:
In the 1970s, a gray box on the shelf or under the truck seat could turn a three-and-a-half-watt CB radio into a voice that buried the channel and came booming out of the neighbors' TV sets. The FCC banned CB linear amplifiers in 1975, banned them harder in 1978, and won in federal court in 1980. So what happened to them?

This is the story of the burners and afterburners CBers bought for under 85 dollars, the TV sweep tubes and self-switching relays inside them, the harmonics that landed on TV channel 2, the 1975 rule that left a door open, the FCC's own 1977 field study that measured the typical linear at about 117 watts and figured catching half of them would take 430 years of agents' time, the February 1978 ban built around 50 watts of drive, the Kenwood ad that skipped ten meters, the ARRL's lawsuit, and why every certified ham amplifier is still built to do nothing between 26 and 28 megahertz.

Did you ever run a burner, or did a neighbor's voice ever come out of your TV? Tell us in the comments. And if a date, a number or a name here doesn't match what you saw at the time, say so below. Good corrections get pinned.

This video was made with the help of AI tools for the narration voice and some period-style illustrations. Historical photos come from Wikimedia Commons and are credited below.

This is the story of the burners and afterburners CBers bought for under 85 dollars, the TV sweep tubes and self-switching relays inside them, the harmonics that landed on TV channel 2, the 1975 rule that left a door open, the FCC's own 1977 field study that measured the typical linear at about 117 watts and figured catching half of them would take 430 years of agents' time, the February 1978 ban built around 50 watts of drive, the Kenwood ad that skipped ten meters, the ARRL's lawsuit, and why every certified ham amplifier is still built to do nothing between 26 and 28 megahertz.

Did you ever run a burner, or did a neighbor's voice ever come out of your TV? Tell us in the comments. And if a date, a number or a name here doesn't match what you saw at the time, say so below. Good corrections get pinned.

snippet.description:
IEEE RF bands divide radio frequencies into ranges based on their applications. Lower bands like HF, VHF and UHF support ham radio, broadcasting and mobile communication. Dipoles, inverted-V antennas, whips and Yagis are common because their wavelengths are relatively long.

As frequency increases into L, S, C and X bands, antennas become smaller. Patch, helical, horn and parabolic antennas support GPS, Wi-Fi, radar and satellites. At Ku, K, Ka, V and W bands, dishes, horns and phased arrays provide focused beams for high-speed communication, sensing and imaging.

snippet.title: This Cheap Fix Made My Portable Vertical Way Stronger
snippet.description:
If your HF-010 (or similar portable vertical) is sitting on the ground, you’re probably losing most of your power to ground loss absorption. In this video I show a simple, low-cost way to elevate the antenna and radials about one meter and jump from roughly 20–35% efficiency to 85% or better — that’s 4 to 5 times more radiated signal with the same radio and the same three radials.

Materials used:
Schedule 40 PVC pipe (~40")
Jubilee/hose clamps
Paracord for guys
Tent stakes
Electric fence posts (or non-conductive driveway markers) for radial ends

All of this is on top of the stock HF-010 kit. One-time tuning per band, then a cheat sheet for future activations. 

POTA activation at Davy Crockett State Park (US-2941) in Tennessee with real on-air results.

Schedule 40 PVC pipe (~40")
Jubilee/hose clamps
Paracord for guys
Tent stakes
Electric fence posts (or non-conductive driveway markers) for radial ends

snippet.title: What Ham Operators Heard The Night Pearl Harbor Was Attacked
snippet.description:
What did amateur radio operators hear on the night Pearl Harbor was attacked?

On December 7, 1941, the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor changed the course of American history. But beyond the official reports and radio broadcasts, amateur radio operators were part of a nationwide network of listeners who followed the airwaves during one of the most dramatic moments of World War II.

In this video, we explore the world of amateur radio during the Pearl Harbor attack, the shortwave broadcasts Americans could hear, the emergency communications that followed, and the role radio enthusiasts played during wartime. We also examine the restrictions imposed on amateur radio operations after the United States entered the war, when civilian transmitting was suspended for national security reasons.

From crackling shortwave signals to the uncertainty of that historic night, discover how radio connected people to a world suddenly at war.

snippet.title: What is the T Index and what does it mean for HF propagation?
snippet.description:
What is the T-Index, and how does it affect HF radio propagation? In this video, we explain one of the lesser-known but valuable indicators of HF propagation conditions for amateur radio (Ham Radio) operators. Discover how the T-Index relates to sunspot numbers, solar activity, the ionosphere and the Maximum Usable Frequency (MUF), and why it can provide a more realistic picture of HF band conditions than sunspot numbers alone. We'll explore how ionosondes measure the ionosphere, what foF2 means, and how Australia's Bureau of Meteorology Space Weather Services uses T-Index data in HF propagation prediction tools such as ASAPS. Whether you're a beginner learning about HF communications or an experienced Ham Radio operator chasing DX, hunting or activating POTA (Parks on the Air) and WWFF (World Wide Flora and Fauna) stations, understanding the T-Index can help you interpret propagation forecasts, choose the best HF frequencies and improve your chances of making long-distance contacts on bands such as 10m, 15m, 20m and 40m.

📻 Enjoying the content? Subscribe to the channel for more practical amateur radio videos covering HF propagation, DXing, radio technology and portable operating. Hit the like button if you found this explanation useful, and share it with a fellow ham who might benefit!

snippet.title: 009 Qué errores comete todo principiante - Lo que nadie te explica cuando empiezas en radio
snippet.description:
Empezar en radioafición es una mezcla de ilusión, curiosidad y, en muchas ocasiones, un poco de miedo a equivocarse.
Encendemos el equipo, escuchamos a otros operadores y parece que todos saben perfectamente qué hacer. Conocen las frecuencias, utilizan palabras que todavía no entendemos y mantienen conversaciones como si llevaran toda la vida haciéndolo.
Y nosotros pensamos:
«¿Cómo voy a hacer yo eso sin meter la pata?»
La respuesta es sencilla: metiendo la pata.
Porque todos los radioaficionados, absolutamente todos, hemos cometido errores cuando empezábamos.
Uno de los más habituales es transmitir sin escuchar primero. Encontramos una frecuencia aparentemente vacía, pulsamos el PTT y comenzamos a hablar. Después descubrimos que había una conversación en marcha que nosotros no conseguíamos escuchar correctamente.
La solución es sencilla: escuchar unos segundos y comprobar que la frecuencia está realmente libre antes de llamar.

Congress banned Russian energy imports—yet three tankers carrying Russian diesel are crossing the Atlantic toward U.S. ports right now, and the Trump administration says the diesel can be legally unloaded while the ban stays in place [00:00:00]. How can both things be true [00:00:06]?

In collaboration with Lawyer Stories, international lawyer Dr. Chad Michael Altieri explains the law behind the headline [00:00:12]. Following President Trump’s agreement with Vladimir Putin, the U.S. Treasury Department issued General License 135—authorizing the sale, delivery, offloading, and importation of Russian diesel through April 7, 2027 to lower transportation and consumer costs [00:00:25].

Discover the constitutional separation-of-powers clash between Congress’s 2022 Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act [00:00:41] and the executive licensing carve-out hidden inside Executive Order 14066 [00:01:11]—plus why U.S. Treasury permission does NOT shield maritime shippers, insurers, and banks from UK, EU, or Canadian sanctions [00:02:00].

Yazdanyar Law Offices specializes in assisting clients nationwide to comply with and address issues related to the sanctions programs administered by the Department of Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).  More specifically, her practice focuses mainly on assisting Iranian-Americans and Legal Permanent Residents of the United States with the legal and transparent transfer of assets from Iran to the United States and/or obtaining specific licenses from OFAC authorizing otherwise prohibited transactions. Yazdanyar Law Offices has successfully defended federally prosecuted clients on issues relating to U.S. trade sanctions, handled OFAC matters arising before the Federal Bureau of Investigations, as well as successfully assisted hundreds of clients throughout the U.S. with the transfer of assets from Iran to the United States.

Our firm works diligently to protect the rights and assets of our clients. Given the broad reach of the current OFAC regulations involving sanctions against Iran, many members of the Iranian-American community have inadvertently found themselves in possible violation of federal laws. At Yazdanyar Law Offices, we make it our priority to educate our community on the current state of the law and to protect our clients against criminal and civil prosecution.
